how_to_use: This is the Canon knowledge selected for this request. It is durable creative and production knowledge — what makes work good and what commonly goes wrong. It says nothing about which image or video model to use, what a provider charges, or whether a model can execute something reliably. Read each item with its `epistemics`: a claim the source hedged is not a rule, a caveat marked extractor_observed is this project's doubt rather than the author's, and a binding marked proposed has not been reviewed by anyone. Items are delivered in full unless `delivered_complete` is false; `detail_ref` fetches the untruncated object in the rare case you need it.

source.title: grammar-of-the-edit-ch3-5 (Roy Thompson, Christopher J. Bowen)
source.lineage_note: Not an independent origin from grammar-of-the-shot-ch4 — the Audit Gate records these as one origin, so agreement between them is not corroboration.

content.claim: The action line, or axis of action, is an imaginary line running through the area of action — along the talent's sight lines, or in the direction an object moves. It establishes a 180 degree arc around the subject and dictates which side the camera may shoot from. The editor must select only shots taken from one side of it, and so maintain the established screen direction, unless the line is seen to change on screen, as when a car changes direction during a shot.
source_words: It is the imaginary line that cuts through the area of action along talent's sight lines or follows in the direction of an object's movement.
The editor must only select shots from one side of the line unless the line is seen to change
content.scope_conditions: assembling coverage of a scene with an established direction of action or attention
source_stated_remedies: select shots from only one side of the line

caveats.text: the source calls the line a mental guide for both directors and editors, so the editor's obligation is to select within constraints production has already fixed
the exception — unless the line is seen to change — puts the burden on the change being visible to the audience, which the source states but does not elaborate

source.title: grammar-of-the-shot-ch4 (Roy Thompson, Christopher J. Bowen)
source.lineage_note: Not an independent origin from grammar-of-the-edit-ch3-5 — the Audit Gate records these as one origin, so agreement between them is not corroboration.

content.claim: Placing the camera on the far side of the action line reverses the established left and right and inverts the film space for the viewer. The resulting shot is perfectly good in itself: the mistake becomes apparent only once the shots are edited together, at which point both characters appear to look the same way rather than at each other.
source_words: To "jump the line" or "cross the line" means that you placed the camera on the opposite side of the action line
the real mistake is not apparent until the three shots are edited together
most filmmakers do not notice it until they get into the editing process
content.mechanism_text: Crossing the line reverses the directions established for the film space, so the cut yields two characters whose attention no longer points at one another.
content.scope_conditions: coverage shot from the far side of an established action line
source_stated_problems: the cuts make no sense because it now appears that both A and B are sitting in the same fashion looking off frame right
inverting the film space on the unaware viewer

caveats.text: the authors state most filmmakers do not notice this until the edit, which asserts the defect is not merely invisible in a frame but reliably missed on set
the figure makes the property directly legible: the erroneous close-up is an unremarkable image, and the fault exists only in its relation to the preceding shot

content.claim: Requests to redesign a logo are often motivated by a desire for change merely for its own sake, which the source calls a very wrong motivation. A real corporate identity rests on an overall system rather than on a logo alone. A logo gradually becomes part of collective culture, and one in the public domain for more than fifty years becomes a classic and a landmark that should not be discarded for a new one however well designed. The source reports proposing a light retouch of the existing mark rather than a replacement when asked to design a new logo for Ford, and doing the same for Ciga Hotels, Cinzano and Lancia.
source_words: A real Corporate Identity is based on an overall system approach, not just a logo.
When a logo has been in the public domain for more than fifty years it becomes a classic, a landmark, a respectable entity
content.mechanism_text: Long public exposure roots a mark in people's consciousness, so the accumulated recognition is itself the asset and replacing the mark discards it.
content.scope_conditions: established marks with long public exposure
source_stated_problems: the desire of change merely for the sake of change
source_stated_remedies: propose a light retouch of an established mark rather than a replacement
treat corporate identity as an overall system rather than as a logo

caveats.text: the source grounds the position partly autobiographically, in having grown up where history and vernacular architecture were treated as protected culture
the fifty-year threshold is stated without derivation; the cases named are all ones where the source's own recommendation was retention

source.title: grammar-of-the-edit-ch3-5 (Roy Thompson, Christopher J. Bowen)
source.lineage_note: Not an independent origin from grammar-of-the-shot-ch4 — the Audit Gate records these as one origin, so agreement between them is not corroboration.

content.label: the_four_continuities
content.description: Continuity is divided by the source into four kinds that must each be addressed separately: content, movement, position and sound. Each has its own failure and, for three of the four, its own remedy.
content.whole_system_claim: The four are treated as one responsibility with four independent failure surfaces. A transition can satisfy any three and fail the fourth, and each failure looks different to the viewer — a mismatched object, a reversed direction of travel, a subject that jumps across the screen, sound that vanishes. Two of the four, movement and position, share a single underlying cause in the geometry of the action line, and the source treats them separately in Chapter Three before supplying the shared cause in Chapter Five.

epistemics.whole_system_claim_interpretation_basis: The division into four and the requirement to address each is the source's own, stated at the head of the Continuity section and repeated in the chapter review. What is ours is the observation that movement and position both reduce to the action line, which the source supplies two chapters later without connecting it back, and the observation that the four are independently failable rather than aspects of one property.
epistemics.system_level_uncertainty: Membership and ordering are the source's own. The grouping of the cut-away as a shared remedy serving two of the four is ours, though it rests on the source using the same action and the same stated mechanism in both places under two names.

relevance.basis: BM25 rank within this object kind. It measures fit to the retrieval question, and says nothing about how good or how well-evidenced the knowledge is.

content.rationale: Judgement is made against an implied viewing scale, and the source states that judging on a miniature systematically distorts it. Its remedy is to reconstruct the delivery conditions artificially — a thousand-seat theatre, a thirty-foot screen, no possibility of further change. The transferable constraint is that an asset should be assessed at its delivery scale, which for this product is a phone in a feed rather than a cinema.
content.applicability_when: deciding the conditions under which a generated asset is reviewed
content.applicability_limits: The source's specific scale is theatrical and its remedy is a physical prop. Only the principle transfers, and this product's delivery scale is smaller than the review scale rather than larger, so the distortion may run the opposite way.

epistemics.binding_status_reason: not reviewed — the inversion of the scale relation for feed-native work is our observation and is untested
epistemics.review_note: This is a proposed use of the knowledge by this project. It is not part of the source's claim.

content.label: devices_by_which_a_reproduced_indian_advertisement_carries_its_whole_argument
content.description: Six devices observed by inspecting the book's plate insert, in which the advertisement's argument is carried by the image and its construction rather than by copy: a familiar everyday scene recruited as the demonstration; a single abstract symbol under an instruction headline; a mascot inserted into a foreign icon set at reduced scale; a fixed form with one variable joke slot; a sung word typeset as the picture; and vernacular appropriation carried simultaneously by word, script and setting.
content.whole_system_claim: Across these executions the verbal load is low or absent and the work is done by what is depicted and how it is arranged — which means a text-only representation of this book would lose the evidence for most of its craft claims, and which also means each device depends on cultural knowledge the viewer must already hold.

tradeoffs.nature: dense documentary photograph versus one abstract symbol — opposite ends of a density range, both carrying the whole argument

epistemics.whole_system_claim_interpretation_basis: The source supplies only a one-line caption per plate and never discusses composition, typography, scale or layout for any of them. Every structural observation in this system was made by CANON-014 opening the images. The grouping asserts a family resemblance the author never proposes. It is offered as a hypothesis about the plates, not as a report of the book.
epistemics.system_level_uncertainty: High, and higher than any member. Each member is an observation about one plate that CANON-014 made first-hand and can be re-checked against the named image file. The claim that the eight constitute one family of devices is entirely the extractor's synthesis over a plate insert the book's own text never analyses. A different reader could group them differently or reject the grouping. This system is a hypothesis about Indian advertising craft, and it must not be consumed as Parameswaran's position — he does not have one on this.

source.title: grammar-of-the-edit-ch3-5 (Roy Thompson, Christopher J. Bowen)
source.lineage_note: Not an independent origin from grammar-of-the-shot-ch4 — the Audit Gate records these as one origin, so agreement between them is not corroboration.

content.claim: Screen direction — whether talent or objects move toward frame left or frame right — must hold across a cut whenever the next shot continues the same movement. Where the available shot contradicts the established direction, the editor must insert a shot that continues the narrative and breaks the audience's attention on the direction of travel.
source_words: Screen direction is the movement of talent or objects toward frame right or frame left. This must be maintained as you transition from one shot to the next
content.scope_conditions: successive shots covering the same movement
source_stated_problems: the shot contradicts the already established screen direction
source_stated_remedies: insert a logical shot that provides a visual break from the discontinuity of movement

caveats.text: the source places responsibility with production, which should have respected screen direction and the 180 degree rule while shooting coverage
the inserted shot is said to offer the audience a break allowing the character time to reverse direction; no reason is given why elapsed screen time makes a reversal acceptable
